title: Voice of Customer: Thematic Asks & Prioritization (June 2025)
content:
Purpose:
Summarize customer feedback collected Apr–May 2025 across onboarding calls, support tickets, CSM check-ins, and product interviews. Group requests into themes, estimate impact, and recommend immediate asks for Eng/Product. This is a working synthesis — intended for cross-functional planning and to inform the June roadmap conversation.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Top themes: latency/cost transparency, model customization (instruction tuning + fine-tunes), rollout/fallback controls, observability/attribution, private deployment onboarding friction.
- Quick wins (2–4 weeks): improved token billing breakdown in Console, clear streaming retry guidance, a templated private-deploy onboarding checklist.
- Medium bets (1–3 months): token-level cost attribution API, model variant auto-fallback UI, lightweight hosted fine-tune flow.
- High-effort strategic (3+ months): self-serve model surgery (small fine-tunes + quantized serving), expanded private region install kit.

Methodology:
- Sources: 42 support threads (Apr–May), 18 post-demo surveys, 9 customer success calls, 3 pilot engagements (healthcare, fintech, commerce).
- Tagging approach: each feedback item tagged by theme and by frequency. Frequency buckets: (H) >=8 mentions, (M) 3–7 mentions, (L) 1–2 mentions.

Thematic breakdown:
1) Latency, cost transparency and token accounting (H)
- Common asks: clearer per-route token cost, per-request latency distributions, and alerting on cost spikes. Several customers confused by batched vs streaming token counts.
- Representative quote: "We saw a 4x cost bump last week and couldn't tell which route generated it — we need per-route token attribution."
- Business impact: high — affects procurement and continued usage.
- Proposed next steps: (a) Console widget showing per-route token and latency histograms (quick UI), (b) API endpoint for per-request token meta (medium).
- Rough effort: UI card (2 sprints frontend + 1 backend), API (3 sprints backend).
- Priority: P0 for Console card, P1 for API.

2) Model customization & control: instruction tuning, fine-tunes, pins (H)
- Common asks: easier workflow to pin a custom-tuned variant, lightweight fine-tune for up to ~50–200k tokens, ability to serve quantized variants automatically.
- Quote: "We need to tweak just a few failure modes for our LLM — full fine-tune is overkill but there's no simple path."
- Impact: medium–high for product-led customers who need small customizations without Dedicated.
- Proposed next steps: pilot a hosted 'micro-tune' flow (CLI + Console) and a pin-management UI.
- Rough effort: pilot (6–8 weeks cross-team).
- Priority: P0 for pin-management UX, P2 for micro-tune pilot depending on infra support.

3) Rollouts, fallback policies, and graceful degradation (M)
- Asks: better canary targeting (route-level), automatic fallback to cheaper model variant under saturation, explicit circuit-breaker settings per route.
- Quote: "When one zone was slow, traffic didn't failover cleanly — latency-sensitive endpoints suffered."
- Proposed next steps: define route-level policy model (policy DSL) and expose simple toggles in Console (auto-fallback on/off, fallback candidate selection).
- Effort: design + 3 sprints eng.
- Priority: P1.

4) Observability & failure attribution (H)
- Asks: token-level traces, sample-level quality metrics, per-request prompt/response retention controls for debugging, and correlation ids surfaced in logs/console.
- Impact: high for SREs and platform teams.
- Quick wins: surface correlation id in Console and SDKs; add a per-request 'example view' that links to logs (with retention note).
- Priority: P0 quick wins; P1 full tracing.

5) Private deployment onboarding friction (M)
- Asks: clearer network prerequisites (firewalls/KMS), step-by-step checklist, sample manifests for common cloud providers, and a shorter pilot checklist for regulated customers.
- Quote: "We stalled for 3 weeks waiting for networking approvals — we need a ready-to-run checklist for security teams."
- Proposed next steps: create a hardened onboarding playbook (docs + exec summary) and a preflight validation script.
- Priority: P0 docs + playbook, P2 preflight script.

6) SDK ergonomics and streaming robustness (M)
- Asks: language idiom updates (Go + Java), clearer streaming reconnection examples, and a single-call 'managed stream' helper.
- Impact: medium — developer experience.
- Quick win: add reconnection snippet to streaming docs and include sample code in Console.
- Priority: P1.

7) Embeddings quality & semantic search tuning (L)
- Asks: more guidance on distance thresholds, sample prompt sets for reranking, and a way to attach metadata to embeddings for downstream attribution.
- Proposed next steps: run a short playbook + guide and include recommended parameters per use case.
- Priority: P2.

Prioritization summary (recommended):
- P0 (near-term): Console token/latency card, correlation id surfacing, onboarding playbook, streaming retry snippet, pin-management UX.
- P1 (next cycle): route fallback policy UI, per-request 'example view', SDK updates (Go/Java), tracing hooks design.
- P2 (medium): per-request token API, micro-tune pilot, preflight validation script, embeddings playbook.
- P3 (longer): full self-serve fine-tune product, expanded private-region installer.

Cross-team asks and riskiest assumptions:
- Infra: need to confirm storage & retention limits for per-request meta (privacy + cost).
- Security/Compliance: private deploy playbook must map to KMS/HSM guides; legal wants a retention rubric.
- Applied ML: micro-tune feasibility depends on latency overhead and kernel compatibility for quantized models.
- Sales/CS: want templated collateral to accelerate procurement once features shipped.

Open questions / items to validate with customers:
- Which customers will pay for micro-tune vs. expect it included in Hosted? (validate willingness to pay)
- How many customers need per-request token history vs aggregated per-route? (cost of ingestion/retention)
- Acceptable default retention windows for prompt/response examples for debugging (30/90/365 days)?

Immediate next steps (owner + timeline):
- CS/Product: run 2 targeted validation calls for micro-tune willingness (owner: Sofia Patel) — in 2 weeks.
- Product/Console: spec Console card + correlation id surfacing (owner: Daniel Kim) — draft in 1 week.
- Docs/SRE: publish private-deploy onboarding playbook (owner: Maya Chen) — 2-week deliverable.
- Eng infra: cost estimate for per-request meta storage (owner: Arjun Rao) — 2 weeks.

Notes to self / informal bits:
- Many customers conflate streaming tokens vs per-request billing; helpful to add a small explainer panel in billing docs.
- Pilot customer A (fintech) extremely price-sensitive — likely to adopt auto-fallback.
- Pilot customer B (healthcare) requires 90-day retention plus SOC2 notes — flag to security.
- Keep thread with "prod-latency-ops" Slack for cross-team updates.

Linked artifacts and references (tickets & pages):
- CONFLUENCE: /display/INF/Token+Attribution+Spike (internal)
- JIRA: INF-728 (token billing UI), INF-742 (correlation-id infra), CS-231 (private-deploy playbook)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/984 (billing-card WIP)

Appendix: raw customer quotes (selected)
- "If we could get automatic fallback to a cheaper model when the premium queue fills, we'd keep it on for high-sensitivity routes."
- "Show me which product route consumed the most tokens this month — procurement needs it."
- "Fine-tunes are all-or-nothing today; we need a stopgap small-tune path."

Status: draft — please add comments inline or ping me in #cs-feedback for urgent corrections.
